paper.title: Contextual Combinatorial Bandits with Changing Action Sets via Gaussian Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual combinatorial multi-armed bandit with changing action sets (C3-MAB), GP-sampled base arm outcomes
unmapped: Base arms are defined by contexts in a compact context space X; mean outcome function f is a sample from a GP with known kernel (k(x,x)<=1)
Available base arms and their contexts change arbitrarily each round (at most M available arms); learner knows M
Expected super-arm reward u is known, monotone and B-Lipschitz (L1) in base arm means
Learner uses an alpha-approximation oracle; regret is alpha-approximation regret
settings.definition_quote: We assume that there exists a function $f:\XX \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, such that we have $r(x)=f(x) +\eta$, for every $x\in \XX$, where $\eta \sim {\cal N} (0,\sigma^2)$. ... we use the standard notion of $\alpha$-approximation regret ... $R_{\alpha} (T) = \alpha \sum^T_{t=1} \textup{opt}(f_t ) - \sum^T_{t=1} u(f( \bs{x}_{t,S_t} ))$.

symbols.B_lip: Lipschitz constant of expected reward u in base arm means (Assumption 2)
symbols.lambda_star: maximum eigenvalue of posterior covariance matrices of selected actions up to T
symbols.M: maximum number of available base arms per round
symbols.gamma_KT: maximum information gain over feasible super-arm context sequences from the arrived context sets

conditions: f sampled from GP with k(x,x) <= 1
|S| <= K (=m) for all feasible super arms

source.label: mainthm
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$, $T \in \mathbb{N}$. Given $\beta_t = 2\log (M\pi^2t^2/ 3\delta )$, the regret incurred by O'CLOK-UCB in $T$ rounds is upper bounded as $R_{\alpha}(T) \leq \sqrt{C(K)K\beta_T T \gamma_{KT}(\mathcal{X}_{\overline{T}})},$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, where $C(K)= 8B^2(\lambda^*(K)+\sigma^2)$, and $\lambda^*(K)$ is the maximum eigenvalue of all covariance matrices of selected actions over $T$ rounds.

results.notes: Paper's K (max super-arm cardinality) mapped to m. Probability is over GP prior and noise. lambda_star is data-dependent. Comparator is per-round optimal super arm scaled by alpha.
